finding.claim: Unauthenticated /fetch2 fetches any http/https URL supplied by the caller, and the only check is a scheme check. An attacker can reach loopback, internal services and cloud metadata (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/), and redirects are followed by default. The first 200 characters of the response are returned to the attacker.

trace.note: url taken directly from the query string
urlparse(url).scheme in ('http','https'), with no host or IP check
requests.get(url) follows redirects by default and returns the body to the caller

finding.guards_checked: is_http_url only checks the scheme. There is no host, IP or private-range block, no redirect restriction, and no auth on the route.

verdict.guard_found: none (is_http_url at validators.py:7 is a scheme-only check; no auth decorator or middleware on /fetch2)
verdict.reason: views.py:19 takes url from the query string, views.py:20 / validators.py:7 only checks the scheme, and views.py:22 calls requests.get(url, timeout=5) with default redirects and returns the first 200 characters of the body, so there is no host or IP guard (unlike /fetch, which uses is_safe_url).

finding.claim: The /fetch SSRF guard has a DNS-rebinding TOCTOU. is_safe_url resolves the hostname with socket.getaddrinfo and checks the IPs, but requests.get then resolves the hostname again independently. An attacker-controlled DNS server can return a public IP for the first lookup and 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254 for the second (TTL 0), which bypasses the check. The response body is returned to the attacker.

trace.note: url taken from the query string
getaddrinfo resolves the host once and checks every returned IP against private, loopback, link-local and reserved ranges
requests.get resolves the hostname again, and the resolved IP is not pinned to the validated one

finding.guards_checked: The scheme allowlist, the private/loopback/link-local/reserved IP check and allow_redirects=False are all present, so redirect-based bypass is blocked. The resolved IP is not pinned, so the rebinding bypass remains. There is no auth on the route.

verdict.guard_found: Scheme allowlist plus a resolved-IP check (private/loopback/link-local/reserved) in is_safe_url at validators.py:12-17, and allow_redirects=False at views.py:14. None of these pin the resolved IP or use a hostname allowlist, so none closes the rebinding bypass.
verdict.reason: validators.py:14 resolves the host via getaddrinfo and checks the IPs, then views.py:14 calls requests.get(url), which resolves the hostname again with no IP pinning. An attacker-controlled DNS server can therefore pass the check and then return 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254. The url comes from request.args at views.py:11 and the route has no auth. One small imprecision: the response body is truncated to 200 characters at views.py:14, which limits what is exposed but does not stop the SSRF.
